name: Typeform
tagline: Polished one-question-at-a-time forms, surveys, quizzes, and lead capture

pricing.notes: Official pricing URL checked; public 2026 references list Basic around $39/month monthly and lower annual pricing.

verdictSummary: A one-question form UI is easy, but Typeform's respondent UX, templates, analytics, integrations, anti-spam, payments, and scale justify a kinda.
coreLoopDIY: Build a form schema/editor, render one question at a time, store responses, export CSV, and send webhooks.
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay because the form looks good and converts without custom QA.

priorArt.name: HeyForm
priorArt.desc: Open-source form builder with surveys and forms; useful prior art for Typeform-like flows.

alternatives.name: HeyForm
alternatives.desc: Typeform's manners, minus the monthly rent

facts.dataFormat: Forms, logic and responses in MongoDB; queues and cache in Redis; uploads use configured server or object storage
facts.gapVsPaid: Its templates, visual refinement, analytics and integration ecosystem are less polished than Typeform's.
facts.setupBlocker: Self-hosting needs Docker, MongoDB, Redis, mail and persistent storage

alternatives.name: Typebot
alternatives.desc: Conversational forms with serious branching; free to self-host under a fair-source licence

facts.engines: OpenAI blocks and other configured AI or API integrations
facts.dataFormat: Bots and responses in PostgreSQL; uploaded files in S3-compatible storage
facts.gapVsPaid: Its chatbot-first builder is excellent for branching conversations but weaker for conventional surveys, quizzes, reporting and Typeform-style presentation.
facts.setupBlocker: Self-hosting needs Docker, PostgreSQL, S3-compatible storage, SMTP and a public domain

alternatives.name: Tally
alternatives.desc: A generous hosted form builder with logic and unlimited responses; branding is the upsell

facts.dataFormat: Forms and submissions live in Tally's cloud; submissions export as CSV or sync to Google Sheets
facts.gapVsPaid: Its free product is generous, but the presentation is less distinctly one-question-at-a-time and branding, custom domains and some team controls are paid.

alternatives.name: OpnForm
alternatives.desc: Open-source forms with unlimited respondents; the free self-hosted builder team stops at two

facts.dataFormat: Form data in PostgreSQL, sessions and queues in Redis, and uploads in local or S3-compatible storage
facts.gapVsPaid: Its conversational presentation, template polish, analytics and integration breadth are less mature than Typeform's.
facts.setupBlocker: Docker plus PostgreSQL, Redis, mail, a domain and persistent or object storage

rejectedAlternatives.name: OhMyForm
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Everyone still recommends it; the repo was archived in 2024 and the last real code is roughly five years old

rejectedAlternatives.name: SurveyJS
rejectedAlternatives.desc: The free part is a JavaScript library; the no-code creator and analytics need paid developer licences

rejectedAlternatives.name: TellForm
rejectedAlternatives.desc: A once-famous Typeform clone; archived since 2019, which is a long time to trust a form endpoint

notes: Useful because Typeform is easy to demo but hard to match in conversion polish.
prompt:
Build me a one-question-at-a-time survey app to replace Typeform, personal scale. Requirements:

- Node + Express + better-sqlite3 on my VPS behind Caddy. A form is a YAML file in
  forms/ (types: text, email, select, rating 1-5, yes/no), loaded at request time.
  No visual builder.
- Public page at /s/<slug>: one question on screen, large type, Enter or click to
  advance, up arrow to go back, progress bar, thank-you screen. Vanilla JS, no
  framework, works on a phone.
- Simple branching: a question may declare next: per answer. One level deep, do not
  build a logic engine.
- Responses saved on completion to SQLite with timestamp and form version.
- CSV export at /admin/<slug>.csv behind an ADMIN_TOKEN from .env; optional webhook
  POST per completed response, URL set in the form's YAML.
- Honeypot field and a per-IP rate limit for spam, nothing fancier.
- No accounts, no telemetry; respondent data stays in my SQLite file.
- Out of scope: a drag-and-drop editor, payments, analytics dashboards, and
  partial-response capture. Adding a form means dropping a YAML file on the server.
- README: Caddy snippet and the YAML form format with one full example.
